text: {"frames":["You grab the wooden spoon just as the soup boils over the rim of the great pot in the Tower kitchen. Steam rolls up the stairwell, and the cook, Sientje-of-the-Dyke, groans over the mess on the stove. The pot still holds {c} ladles of thick pea soup for the watchmen waiting below. Each watchman must get the same amount, with nobody given a drop more than the others. How many ladles does each watchman get when the soup is cut into equal halves?","Stuck fast, shouts the peat barge skipper on the canal below the Tower. His barge is heavy with {c} sacks of black peat, and the lock keeper, Joost Mallemolen, says the load must be split evenly before the barge can float free. The sacks go onto the two carts on the quay, and each cart must carry the same weight. How many sacks must go on each cart so the barge can slip out of the mud?","A stork has built a nest of straw on the mill sail, and the sail will not turn. The miller, Wiebe Millsail, climbs up the ladder and finds {c} heavy bundles tied to the frame. He must move them so both sides of the sail weigh the same, or the mill will never grind again. How many bundles should he take from the heavier side to balance the sail?","Something is missing from the cupboard on the third floor: the honey jar is empty, and a steady hum comes from behind the linen. Bees have moved in and filled a comb with honey, and it holds {c} sealed cells. The tailor, Trijntje Klomp, wants half of the comb for her bread and the bees may keep the other half. How many cells does she take?","Smoke and burnt sugar drift up the stairwell from the bakery on the ground floor. The baker has burnt a tray of rolls, but {c} rolls came out golden and whole. The watchman and the tailor are both hungry, and the baker wants to give them the good rolls in equal shares. How many good rolls does each of them get?"]}
